doc.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Schoolhouse Rock and Conjunction Junction
summary: Singing Schoolhouse Rock songs written by Dorough and Frishberg, the link to The Simpsons.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let me ask you about a few of the records you’ve played on. I’m going to work backwards here because I spotted something about “The Simpsons?”
Oh yeah. Well that was because of “Conjunction Junction.” That’s something that I did that got real famous, with all the “Schoolhouse Rock” things.
Oh yeah. I didn’t know you were on that.

Well I sing “Conjunction Junction” and “I’m Just a Bill” and whole bunch of those things, because of Bob Dorough and Dave Frishberg. They started writing them twenty years ago or so. The first one we did was “Conjunction Junction.” And I played the trumpet. We layed down a track first and then I sang it. Teddy Edwards and I.
